features.name: Malda / Ganga
features.fact: on Oct 8 the state government announced ₹1.8 lakh per fully damaged home in flood-hit Malda, and IIT Kanpur was tasked with a permanent flood-solution report. The floods followed the Ganga breaching the ring embankment on Bhutni island in early September.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Ganga at Malda — Bhutni diara and Manikchak, Malda district, West Bengal. Malda lies on the Ganga in northern West Bengal, with Bangladesh's Chapainawabganj across the river to the east; the Farakka barrage lies downstream to the south-east.

features.name: Western Ghats (ESA)
features.fact: on Sep 30 the Karnataka legislature unanimously opposed the ESA recommendations in their present form, after the Centre reissued the draft on Jul 27.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Western Ghats — the draft Ecologically Sensitive Area (ESA), six states. The Ghats run parallel to the west coast from the Tapi valley to Kanyakumari, with the Deccan plateau to the east. The July 2026 draft covers about 56,826 sq km across Karnataka (largest share), Kerala (including Wayanad villages), Goa, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Gujarat.

features.name: Srinagar Airport
features.fact: flight operations were reported suspended from Oct 1 to Oct 16 for essential work.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Srinagar airport — Jhelum valley, Jammu & Kashmir. Srinagar sits on the Jhelum in the Kashmir valley, between the Pir Panjal (south) and the Zabarwan hills near Dal Lake.

features.name: Mobile Bay / Gulf Coast
features.fact: Hurricane Isaias, the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 (formed Oct 8, the latest first hurricane in 121 years), strengthened to Category 3 (120 mph) on Oct 9 and was forecast to make landfall on Friday night, Oct 9, between Mobile Bay and the Florida Panhandle.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Gulf Coast — Mobile Bay (Alabama) to Choctawhatchee Bay (Florida Panhandle), USA. Pensacola and Dauphin Island lie nearby on the northern Gulf of Mexico, with the Mississippi coast to the west.

features.name: Mount Ibu
features.fact: per a Databoks report, it erupted repeatedly on Oct 8 (ash to about 400 m above the summit) and logged 27 eruptions in the week to that date. It remains at Level II (Alert), with a 2 km exclusion zone and an extended 3.5 km zone to the north.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Mount Ibu — West Halmahera, North Maluku, Indonesia. On the Halmahera island in the Molucca Sea region of eastern Indonesia, with Ternate and Tidore lying to the west.

features.name: Mount Semeru
features.fact: it is at Level III (Alert) after repeated eruptions through Oct 1–10. Authorities bar all activity within 13 km in the south-east sector, and pyroclastic surges and lahars may reach 17 km from the summit.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Mount Semeru — Lumajang, East Java, Indonesia. The highest peak of Java, lying south of the Tengger caldera (Bromo is to its north-east), draining south towards the Indian Ocean through the Besuk Kobokan river.

features.name: Ili Lewotolok
features.fact: ash eruptions were reported on Oct 2, with a 2 km exclusion zone (3 km to the south and south-east).
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Ili Lewotolok — Lembata Island, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. In the Lesser Sundas, east of Flores, with Adonara and Solor lying between them.

features.name: Tambolaka / Sumba
features.fact: a magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck about 39 km WSW of Tambolaka on Oct 3 at 46 km depth; USGS PAGER gave a green alert, meaning limited damage was expected.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Tambolaka, Sumba Island — East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. Sumba lies south of Flores across the Sumba Strait, facing the Indian Ocean to the south.

features.name: Campi Flegrei
features.fact: a Md 4.7 quake on Jul 31 damaged buildings and disrupted transport; INGV counted 428 earthquakes in August (largest Md 3.4, on Aug 10), with uplift of about 10 mm per month.
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Campi Flegrei — Phlegraean Fields, west of Naples, Italy. A restless caldera around the Gulf of Pozzuoli, with Vesuvius to the south-east and Ischia and Procida to the west.

features.name: Mount Olympus
features.fact: the wider area of Mount Olympus was inscribed as a mixed natural–cultural World Heritage Site at the 48th World Heritage Committee, Busan (July 2026).
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Mount Olympus (Greece) — Pieria–Thessaly border, northern Greece. Mytikas, the highest peak, rises above the Aegean, south of the Thermaic Gulf, near Litochoro.

features.name: Boma–Badingilo
features.fact: inscribed in July 2026 as South Sudan's first World Heritage Site (the same session also added Comoros and São Tomé and Príncipe for the first time).
features.locate: Approximate study anchor. Boma–Badingilo Migratory Landscape — south-eastern South Sudan. Boma lies in the east, close to the Ethiopian border between the White Nile and the Ethiopian highlands; Badingilo lies to the west, joined by a savannah corridor.
